title.en: Reduced Relative Clauses (the man sitting there, the book written by …, the first to arrive)
title.es: Las oraciones de relativo reducidas (the man sitting there, the book written by …, the first to arrive)

text.en: A relative clause can be shortened: “who/which + be” can be dropped and the verb stays in the -ing form or as a past participle. Instead of “the man who is sitting there” you say “the man sitting there”, instead of “the book which was written by Orwell” you say “the book written by Orwell”. After “first, last, only” comes a to-infinitive: “the first person to arrive”. The long Spanish “el hombre que está sentado ahí” is said in English with a short participle.
text.es: Una oración de relativo se puede acortar: «who/which + be» se puede omitir y el verbo queda en forma -ing o como participio pasado. En lugar de «the man who is sitting there» se dice «the man sitting there», en lugar de «the book which was written by Orwell» se dice «the book written by Orwell». Después de «first, last, only» va un to-infinitivo: «the first person to arrive». El largo «el hombre que está sentado ahí» del español se dice en inglés con un participio corto.

rows: el hombre sentado ahí (the man ___ there)
el libro escrito por Orwell (the book ___ by Orwell)
la primera en llegar (the first person ___ arrive)
los carros hechos en México (cars ___ in Mexico)
la persona que vive al lado (the person ___ next door)

text.en: It replaces who + be + -ing or who + a present verb: “The girl sitting next to me” = the girl who is sitting next to me; “people living in cities” = people who live in cities.
text.es: Reemplaza a who + be + -ing o who + un verbo en presente: «The girl sitting next to me» = the girl who is sitting next to me; «people living in cities» = people who live in cities.

tr.en: People living in big cities often feel lonely.

title.en: The past participle: a passive meaning

text.en: It replaces which/that + be + participle: “The book written by Orwell” = the book which was written by Orwell; “cars made in Mexico” = cars which are made in Mexico.
text.es: Reemplaza a which/that + be + participio: «The book written by Orwell» = the book which was written by Orwell; «cars made in Mexico» = cars which are made in Mexico.

examples.es: The book written by Orwell is a classic.

tr.en: The book written by Orwell is a classic.
tr.es: El libro escrito por Orwell es un clásico.

examples.es: Cars made in Mexico are sold abroad.

tr.en: Cars made in Mexico are sold abroad.
tr.es: Los carros hechos en México se venden en el extranjero.

title.en: The to-infinitive: first, last, only, superlatives
title.es: El to-infinitivo: first, last, only, superlativos

text.en: After the first / the last / the only / the next / a superlative comes a to-infinitive: “the first person to arrive”, “the only one to know”, “the best way to learn”. Also useful: “something to eat”, “a place to stay”.
text.es: Después de the first / the last / the only / the next / un superlativo va un to-infinitivo: «the first person to arrive», «the only one to know», «the best way to learn». También útil: «something to eat», «a place to stay».

examples.es: The first person to arrive gets a prize.

tr.en: The first person to arrive gets a prize.
tr.es: La primera persona en llegar recibe un premio.

examples.es: She is the only student to pass the exam.

tr.en: She is the only student to pass the exam.
tr.es: Ella es la única estudiante que aprobó el examen.

text.en: Common in official texts: “Anyone wishing to apply should contact the office.” “All passengers traveling to Madrid…” The shortening does not work in every case: a finished past event does not take -ing (“the man who called yesterday”, not “the man calling yesterday”).
text.es: Es común en textos oficiales: «Anyone wishing to apply should contact the office.» «All passengers traveling to Madrid…» El acortamiento no sirve en todos los casos: un hecho pasado terminado no lleva -ing («the man who called yesterday», no «the man calling yesterday»).

examples.es: Anyone wishing to apply should contact the office.

tr.en: Anyone wishing to apply should contact the office.
tr.es: Quien desee postularse debe comunicarse con la oficina.

examples.es: The letter sent yesterday has not arrived.

tr.en: The letter sent yesterday has not arrived.
tr.es: La carta enviada ayer todavía no llega.

text.en: Not “the man sit there”, but “the man sitting there”. In the shortened form there is no finite verb: neither “the man sits there is” nor “the book was written by Orwell is”.
text.es: No «the man sit there», sino «the man sitting there». En la forma acortada no hay un verbo conjugado: ni «the man sits there is» ni «the book was written by Orwell is».

text.en: The -ing form marks something happening at the same time or a general truth; the past participle is passive. The man who called yesterday: “the man who called yesterday”, not “the man calling yesterday”.
text.es: La forma -ing marca algo simultáneo o una verdad general; el participio pasado es pasivo. El hombre que llamó ayer: «the man who called yesterday», no «the man calling yesterday».

speak.en: A relative clause can be shortened. The -ing form has an active meaning: «The man sitting there is my boss». The past participle has a passive meaning: «The book written by Orwell is a classic». After «first, last, only» and a superlative comes a to-infinitive: «The first person to arrive gets a prize». Common in official texts: «Anyone wishing to apply should contact the office». A finished past event cannot be shortened with -ing.
speak.es: Una oración de relativo se puede acortar. La forma -ing tiene sentido activo: «The man sitting there is my boss». El participio pasado tiene sentido pasivo: «The book written by Orwell is a classic». Después de «first, last, only» y de un superlativo va un to-infinitivo: «The first person to arrive gets a prize». Es común en textos oficiales: «Anyone wishing to apply should contact the office». Un hecho pasado terminado no se puede acortar con -ing.

items.sentence: The girl ___ next to me is my cousin.

why.en: An active meaning: the girl sitting next to me.
why.es: Un sentido activo: the girl sitting next to me.

sit.en: “The girl sit next to me” is not correct; you need the -ing form.
sit.es: «The girl sit next to me» no es correcto; hace falta la forma -ing.

to sit.en: “To sit” would express a purpose or a rule; here the girl is already sitting.
to sit.es: «To sit» expresaría una finalidad o una regla; aquí la chica ya está sentada.

examples: The boy standing there is Tom.
The man reading is my uncle.

tr.en: The girl sitting next to me is my cousin.
tr.es: La niña que está sentada junto a mí es mi prima.

items.sentence: The book ___ by Orwell is a classic.

why.en: A passive meaning: the book written by Orwell.
why.es: Un sentido pasivo: the book written by Orwell.

writing.en: “Writing” would mean the book writes; you need a passive.
writing.es: «Writing» significaría que el libro escribe; hace falta una pasiva.

wrote.en: “Wrote by Orwell” is not correct; you need the participle (written).
wrote.es: «Wrote by Orwell» no es correcto; hace falta el participio (written).

examples: The song sung by her is old.
The house built by him is big.

tr.en: The book written by Orwell is a classic.
tr.es: El libro escrito por Orwell es un clásico.

items.sentence: The first person ___ arrive gets a prize.

why.en: After the first comes a to-infinitive: the first person to arrive.
why.es: Después de the first va un to-infinitivo: the first person to arrive.

who.en: “Who arrive” is not correct; after who you would need a finite verb (arrives).
who.es: «Who arrive» no es correcto; después de who haría falta un verbo conjugado (arrives).

for.en: “For arrive” is not correct; you need to.
for.es: «For arrive» no es correcto; hace falta to.

examples: The last man to leave was Tom.
The next train to arrive is late.

tr.en: The first person to arrive gets a prize.
tr.es: La primera persona en llegar recibe un premio.

items.sentence: Cars ___ in Mexico are sold abroad.

why.en: A passive meaning: cars made in Mexico.
why.es: Un sentido pasivo: cars made in Mexico.

making.en: “Making” would mean the cars make something; you need a passive.
making.es: «Making» significaría que los carros fabrican algo; hace falta una pasiva.

make.en: “Cars make in Mexico” is not correct; you need the participle (made).
make.es: «Cars make in Mexico» no es correcto; hace falta el participio (made).

examples: Food cooked at home is cheap.
Goods sold here are new.

tr.en: Cars made in Mexico are sold abroad.
tr.es: Los carros hechos en México se venden en el extranjero.

items.sentence: Anyone ___ to join should call us.

why.en: A formal shortening: anyone wanting to join.
why.es: Un acortamiento formal: anyone wanting to join.

wants.en: “Wants” would put two finite verbs together (wants … should call); you need the -ing form.
wants.es: «Wants» pondría dos verbos conjugados juntos (wants … should call); hace falta la forma -ing.

want.en: “Want” would put two finite verbs together; you need the -ing form.
want.es: «Want» pondría dos verbos conjugados juntos; hace falta la forma -ing.

examples: Anyone wishing to leave may go.
Anyone needing help can ask.

tr.en: Anyone wanting to join should call us.
tr.es: Cualquiera que quiera unirse debe llamarnos.

items.sentence: The woman ___ next door is a teacher.

why.en: An active meaning: the woman living next door.
why.es: Un sentido activo: the woman living next door.

lived.en: “The woman lived next door is” is not correct; two finite verbs would stand together.
lived.es: «The woman lived next door is» no es correcto; irían juntos dos verbos conjugados.

lives.en: “The woman lives next door is” is not correct; two finite verbs would stand together.
lives.es: «The woman lives next door is» no es correcto; irían juntos dos verbos conjugados.

examples: The man working here is kind.
The girl waiting outside is Eva.

tr.en: The woman living next door is a teacher.
tr.es: La mujer que vive al lado es maestra.

items.sentence: The letter ___ yesterday has not arrived.

why.en: A finished, passive meaning: the letter sent yesterday.
why.es: Un sentido terminado y pasivo: the letter sent yesterday.

sending.en: “Sending” would mean the letter sends; you need a passive.
sending.es: «Sending» significaría que la carta envía; hace falta una pasiva.

sends.en: “Sends” would put two finite verbs together; you need a participle.
sends.es: «Sends» pondría dos verbos conjugados juntos; hace falta un participio.

examples: The money paid last week is gone.
The report written today is long.

tr.en: The letter sent yesterday has not arrived.
tr.es: La carta enviada ayer no ha llegado.

items.sentence: She is the only student ___ the exam.

why.en: After the only comes a to-infinitive.
why.es: Después de the only va un to-infinitivo.

pass.en: “The only student pass” is not correct; the to cannot be dropped.
pass.es: «The only student pass» no es correcto; el to no se puede omitir.

passes.en: “Passes” would put two finite verbs together (is … passes); you need the to-infinitive.
passes.es: «Passes» pondría dos verbos conjugados juntos (is … passes); hace falta el to-infinitivo.

examples: He is the only one to know.
She was the first to win.

tr.en: She is the only student to pass the exam.
tr.es: Ella es la única estudiante que pasó el examen.

items.sentence: The best way ___ learn a language is daily practice.

why.en: After the best way comes a to-infinitive.
why.es: Después de the best way va un to-infinitivo.

for.en: “Best way for learn” is not correct; you need to (for + verb does not stand).
for.es: «Best way for learn» no es correcto; hace falta to (for + verbo no va).

of.en: “Best way of learn” is not correct; after of you need -ing, here to + base verb is usual.
of.es: «Best way of learn» no es correcto; después de of hace falta -ing, aquí lo habitual es to + verbo base.

examples: The best time to go is now.
The easiest way to start is here.

tr.en: The best way to learn a language is daily practice.
tr.es: La mejor manera de aprender un idioma es la práctica diaria.

items.sentence: People ___ in big cities often feel lonely.

why.en: A general truth, an active meaning: people living in big cities.
why.es: Una verdad general, un sentido activo: people living in big cities.

lived.en: “People lived in big cities often feel” is not correct; two finite verbs would stand together.
lived.es: «People lived in big cities often feel» no es correcto; irían juntos dos verbos conjugados.

live.en: “People live in big cities often feel” is not correct; two finite verbs would stand together.
live.es: «People live in big cities often feel» no es correcto; irían juntos dos verbos conjugados.

examples: Students studying here are happy.
Workers living far away drive.

tr.en: People living in big cities often feel lonely.
tr.es: La gente que vive en las grandes ciudades a menudo se siente sola.

items.sentence: The documents ___ on the desk are mine.

why.en: An active meaning: the documents lying on the desk.
why.es: Un sentido activo: the documents lying on the desk.

lie.en: “The documents lie on the desk are” is not correct; you need the -ing form.
lie.es: «The documents lie on the desk are» no es correcto; hace falta la forma -ing.

lies.en: “Lies” would put two finite verbs together; you need the -ing form.
lies.es: «Lies» pondría dos verbos conjugados juntos; hace falta la forma -ing.

examples: The cat sleeping there is mine.
The keys lying here are his.

tr.en: The documents lying on the desk are mine.
tr.es: Los documentos que están sobre el escritorio son míos.

items.sentence: Passengers ___ to Madrid should go to gate five.

why.en: An official, active shortening: passengers traveling to Madrid.
why.es: Un acortamiento oficial y activo: passengers traveling to Madrid.

traveled.en: “Passengers traveled to Madrid should” is not correct; you need the -ing form.
traveled.es: «Passengers traveled to Madrid should» no es correcto; hace falta la forma -ing.

travel.en: “Passengers travel to Madrid should” is not correct; you need the -ing form.
travel.es: «Passengers travel to Madrid should» no es correcto; hace falta la forma -ing.

examples: Visitors arriving late must call.
Guests staying here pay less.

tr.en: Passengers traveling to Madrid should go to gate five.
tr.es: Los pasajeros que viajan a Madrid deben ir a la puerta cinco.

items.sentence: He was the last man ___ the building.

why.en: After the last comes a to-infinitive.
why.es: Después de the last va un to-infinitivo.

leave.en: “The last man leave” is not correct; the to cannot be dropped.
leave.es: «The last man leave» no es correcto; el to no se puede omitir.

leaves.en: “Leaves” would put two finite verbs together (was … leaves); you need the to-infinitive.
leaves.es: «Leaves» pondría dos verbos conjugados juntos (was … leaves); hace falta el to-infinitivo.

examples: She was the last to speak.
He was the first to go.

tr.en: He was the last man to leave the building.
tr.es: Él fue el último hombre en salir del edificio.

why.en: A needed person: someone to + base verb.
why.es: Una persona necesaria: someone to + verbo base.

update.en: “Someone update” is not correct; the to cannot be dropped.
update.es: «Someone update» no es correcto; el to no se puede omitir.

updates.en: “Someone updates” would put two finite verbs together; you need the to-infinitive.
updates.es: «Someone updates» pondría dos verbos conjugados juntos; hace falta el to-infinitivo.

examples: We need someone to help.
I want something to eat.

tr.en: We need someone to update the website.
tr.es: Necesitamos a alguien que actualice el sitio web.

items.sentence: The man ___ me directions at the moment is very polite.

why.en: A simultaneous, active meaning: the man giving me directions.
why.es: Un sentido simultáneo y activo: the man giving me directions.

gave.en: “The man gave me directions at the moment is” would put two finite verbs together; you need the -ing form.
gave.es: «The man gave me directions at the moment is» pondría dos verbos conjugados juntos; hace falta la forma -ing.

to give.en: “The man to give me” is not correct in this meaning; you need the -ing form.
to give.es: «The man to give me» no es correcto en este sentido; hace falta la forma -ing.

examples: The woman telling the story is Ann.
The boy helping me is Tom.

tr.en: The man giving me directions at the moment is very polite.
tr.es: El hombre que me está dando indicaciones en este momento es muy educado.

items.sentence: All the students ___ the exam today will receive a certificate.

why.en: An active meaning: all the students passing the exam.
why.es: Un sentido activo: all the students passing the exam.

passed.en: “Passed the exam today will receive” would put two finite verbs together; you need the -ing form.
passed.es: «Passed the exam today will receive» pondría dos verbos conjugados juntos; hace falta la forma -ing.

pass.en: “Pass the exam today will receive” would put two finite verbs together; you need the -ing form.
pass.es: «Pass the exam today will receive» pondría dos verbos conjugados juntos; hace falta la forma -ing.

examples: All guests attending get a gift.
Everyone making it wins.

tr.en: All the students passing the exam today will receive a certificate.
tr.es: Todos los estudiantes que aprueben el examen hoy recibirán un certificado.

items.sentence: The house ___ at the end of the street belongs to my uncle.

why.en: An active meaning: the house standing at the end.
why.es: Un sentido activo: the house standing at the end.

stood.en: “The house stood at the end belongs” would put two finite verbs together; you need the -ing form.
stood.es: «The house stood at the end belongs» pondría dos verbos conjugados juntos; hace falta la forma -ing.

stands.en: “Stands” would put two finite verbs together; you need the -ing form.
stands.es: «Stands» pondría dos verbos conjugados juntos; hace falta la forma -ing.

examples: The tree growing here is old.
The shop standing there is mine.

tr.en: The house standing at the end of the street belongs to my uncle.
tr.es: La casa que está al final de la calle es de mi tío.
